name: TLV7041DCKR
title: Single, dual and quad nanopower 1.6 V to 6.5 V comparators, rail-to-rail inputs, push-pull or open-drain output (TLV7031, TLV7032, TLV7034, TLV7041, TLV7042, TLV7044)
summary: A family of nanopower comparators drawing about 315 nA per channel (335 nA on the singles) with a 3 µs propagation delay. They run from 1.6 V to 6.5 V, take inputs from VEE to 100 mV above VCC without output phase reversal, and have hysteresis built in. TLV703x parts have push-pull outputs; TLV704x parts have open-drain outputs that can be pulled up to 6.5 V regardless of the supply. Singles, duals and quads come in packages down to a 0.8 mm × 0.8 mm X2SON. TLV7041DCKR is the open-drain single in a 5-pin SC70.

circuits.title: TLV703x inverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: The signal goes to IN-. IN+ sits at VA, the tap of R1 (from +5 V) and R2 (to ground), and R3 feeds the output back to that tap. While the output is high R3 is effectively in parallel with R1 and VA is the upper trip point VA1; once the output is low R3 sits in parallel with R2 and VA drops to VA2. With all three resistors 1 MΩ the output goes low as VIN rises past 3.33 V and high again when VIN falls under 1.67 V. RLOAD, 100 kΩ, loads the output.
notes: The trip-point equations take the output high level as VCC.

circuits.title: TLV703x noninverting comparator with hysteresis
circuits.description: IN- is held at VREF, 2.5 V. The input reaches IN+ through R1, 330 kΩ, and R2, 1 MΩ, runs from the output back to IN+. The output switches high when VIN climbs to VIN1, 3.325 V, and switches low when VIN falls to VIN2, 1.675 V, on a 5 V supply. RLOAD loads the output.

circuits.title: TLV704x window comparator
circuits.description: Three equal 10 MΩ resistors in series across the 3.3 V rail make 2.2 V (VTH+) between R1 and R2 and 1.1 V (VTH-) between R2 and R3. The sensor feeds IN- of U1, whose IN+ is at VTH+, and IN+ of U2, whose IN- is at VTH-. The two open-drain outputs are tied together with one pull-up, RPU, into the microcontroller's UV_OV input. UV_OV is high while the sensor is between 1.1 V and 2.2 V and pulled low when it is under 1.1 V or over 2.2 V. The high resistor values keep the divider current small.
notes: Both comparators run with VCC at 3.3 V and VEE at ground.

circuits.title: IR receiver analog front end using TLV7031
circuits.description: An IR LED, reverse biased from the 3 V cell, works as the light sensor; its current through R1, 10 MΩ, makes VIN on IN-. R2 and C1 (470 kΩ and 0.01 µF) average VIN into Vref, which follows the mean level of the IR signal. Vref reaches IN+ through R3, and R4, 10 MΩ, from the output to IN+ adds hysteresis against false toggles. VOUT goes to a microcontroller and can also wake it. The R2-C1 time constant is chosen for the target data rate of 9600 baud; the low bias current is what lets R1 be so large.

parts.note: Reverse biased, used as the receiver.

parts.value: Output to MCU (also to wake-up MCU)

circuits.title: Square-wave oscillator
circuits.description: A relaxation oscillator. R1 from V+, R2 to ground and R3 from the output set VA on IN+, so the threshold steps between VA1 and VA2 as the output changes state. C1 on IN- charges through R4 from the output until VC reaches VA1; the output then falls and C1 discharges through R4 to VA2, when the output rises again. With R1 = R2 = R3 the thresholds are 2/3 and 1/3 of VCC and the frequency is 1 / (2 R4 C1 ln2).
notes: Values with the waveform curve: R1 = R2 = R3 = R4 = 100 kΩ, C1 = 100 pF, a 20 pF output load, V+ = 5 V, V- at ground and 10 pF stray from VA to ground.
The top frequency is set by the propagation delay and the load capacitance on the output; the low bias current allows a small C1 with a large R4.

circuits.title: Quadrature rotary encoder detector with TLV7032
circuits.description: A TMR rotation sensor on 5.5 V gives SIN and COS digital outputs 90° apart. Each output is divided by 100 kΩ over 24.9 kΩ, about one fifth, into IN+ of one TLV7032 channel; both IN- pins sit at a 0.525 V reference, half the 1.05 V the divided high level reaches at minimum. Dividing the input by five makes the 10 mV internal hysteresis act as about 50 mV at the sensor. The comparator outputs drive A and B of a 2-to-4 line decoder whose Y3 to Y0 outputs name the quadrant: 0°-90°, 90°-180°, 180°-270°, 270°-360°. The TLV7032 runs from 3.3 V.
notes: The sensor's minimum output high level is 5.25 V; R2 / (R1 + R2) is set to 1/5.
With R1 = 100 kΩ, R2 = 24.9 kΩ and VREF = 0.525 V the DC input sweep shows about 50 mV of hysteresis.

operation.text: TLV7031 and TLV7041 are single comparators, TLV7032 and TLV7042 duals, TLV7034 and TLV7044 quads. TLV703x parts have a push-pull output that sources and sinks milliamps, enough for an LED or a capacitive load. TLV704x parts have an open-drain output that can be pulled above VCC, for level translation and bipolar-to-single-ended conversion. All have rail-to-rail inputs, built-in hysteresis, no output phase reversal with overdriven inputs, about 315 nA supply current and 3 µs propagation delay, from 1.6 V to 6.5 V and -40 °C to 125 °C. TLV7041DCKR is the open-drain single in SC70 on a 3000-piece reel, marked 19Q.

TLV70x1S and TLV70x1L are the singles with other pin orders, and they work down to a 1.2 V supply. The L pinout, with the supplies reversed from the standard order, replaces LMC72xx and TLV7211 parts in older designs; it is not meant for new designs, where TLV70x1 or TLV70x1S is the choice.

A power-on-reset circuit is active whenever VS is below the minimum supply voltage, on the way up or down. While it is active a TLV703x holds its output low at VEE and a TLV704x leaves its output high impedance, a logic high. Once VS reaches the minimum supply the output follows the differential input. VCC must stay above 1.6 V for the power-up time, 200 µs (400 µs on the quad), before the output is valid.

Common-mode range: VEE to VCC + 100 mV; any differential voltage within it is allowed, and inputs past either rail do not invert the output. The inputs are fault tolerant: their impedance stays high with VCC unpowered or ramping, they accept up to the 7 V absolute maximum with VCC = 0 V, and VCC stays isolated from an input held above it. Typical bias current is 1 pA with the inputs between the rails. Below VEE the internal protection diodes to VEE conduct and bias current grows exponentially. Bias current typically doubles per 10 °C.

The switching point is the threshold voltage VTH plus the offset VOS; the internal hysteresis VHYST forms a window centred on it, so the output trips at VTH + VOS + VHYST / 2 and VTH + VOS - VHYST / 2, which reduces noise sensitivity. VHYST is 7 mV for TLV703x and TLV704x alike. Offset and hysteresis are counted within both tPLH and tPHL. External positive feedback adds hysteresis beyond the internal amount.

The TLV703x push-pull output needs no pull-up resistor and has no shoot-through current. The TLV704x open-drain output can be pulled up to a separate source of up to 6.5 V regardless of the supply voltage, and outputs can be wire-ORed. Pull-up resistance RP is not to be less than 650 Ω on the dual and quad.

VS is VCC - VEE, 1.6 V to 6.5 V, so a single supply (5 V and 0 V) and a split supply (+2.5 V and -2.5 V) give the same operating voltage. With a split supply the output low level is VEE. Capacitive load on the output and a high toggle rate raise the average supply current above the quiescent figure.

X2SON: one 4-mil via in the centre (VEE) pad, tied to a ground plane or trace on the bottom layer, lowers board cost and raises reliability. A 100 nF supply bypass capacitor, placed from the supply pin directly to ground, is called for with a high-impedance or noisy supply, long supply runs, or an output loaded by a long trace or a capacitance; fast output edges and high sink and source drive pull supply current above the quiescent level. In the X2SON layout example the 0.1 µF capacitor sits at the VCC pad and the centre pad reaches a bottom-layer trace through a 4-mil via, then an 8-mil via. The DSG and RTE thermal pads connect to V-, and each is soldered to the board for heat and mechanical strength.

VCC is 3.3 V and VEE ground; R1, R2 and R3 are each 10 MΩ, so VTH+ is 2.2 V and VTH- 1.1 V. The open-drain TLV704x is used so the two outputs can share one line; each output goes low when the sensor is below 1.1 V or above 2.2 V, and the line is high between them.

The target hysteresis is 50 mV. Since the TLV7032 has 10 mV typical internal hysteresis, the sensor output is divided by five, which scales the effective hysteresis up by five. The sensor's minimum high output, 5.25 V, is the divider input; R1 = 100 kΩ and R2 = 24.9 kΩ give 1.05 V minimum at IN+ when the sensor is high, and IN- is tied to 0.525 V so the switching point is at half the high level. The same approach suits optical, capacitive or inductive sensors.
AEC-Q100 qualified versions are TLV7031-Q1, TLV7032-Q1, TLV7034-Q1, TLV7041-Q1, TLV7042-Q1 and TLV7044-Q1.
